title: Chicken breast, baked, coated, skin/coating not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken breast is a lean, boneless cut of meat rich in protein. In this form it is baked, coated with a breading, and the skin and coating are not consumed. This preparation retains most nutrients while providing a convenient, ready‑to‑eat option.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast provides about 31 g of protein per 100 g.
Baking without added fat makes it more diet‑friendly than frying.
The coating is often made from whole‑grain flour or breadcrumbs, adding a small amount of carbs and fiber.
Chicken is a good source of vitamin B6, which supports amino‑acid metabolism.
When baked at 180 °C the breast stays moist and juicy.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Protein is essential for muscle growth, repair, and immune function.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Skin‑less baked breast contains little saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 aids protein metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: With minimal carbohydrates, it does not cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor harmful bacteria; ensure proper cooking temperature.

items.title: Sodium in the coating
items.content: Prepared breadings often contain salt; choose low‑sodium versions if needed.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some ready‑made coatings may include preservatives or flavor enhancers that not everyone tolerates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the breast and add it to salads, sandwiches, or wraps. It works well in quick meals such as pasta, rice bowls, or vegetable stir‑fries. If the coating is not edible, remove it before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked breast in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it remains good for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.
